The set of vertices in the second line is part of at least one optimal solution with cost s.
The cost s is the minimum possible cost to guarantee Arkady's win.

candidate_issues.instruction: Add a postcondition to ensure that the output vertices are exactly those that appear in at least one optimal set (not just a subset). The current Q4 only checks if the output is part of an optimal set, but does not enforce that it includes all vertices that must appear in at least one optimal set.
candidate_issues.task_evidence: Also, we ask you to find all such vertices that there is an optimal (i.e. with cost s) set of vertices containing this one such that Arkady can guarantee his own win buying this set on the first stage.

candidate_issues.instruction: Add a postcondition to ensure that the cost `s` is computed correctly as the minimum total cost to guarantee Arkady's win for all possible integer assignments by Vasily. The current Q5 only checks if `s` is the minimum cost, but does not explicitly verify the correctness of the underlying logic (e.g., whether the chosen vertices can indeed guarantee zeroing all leaves for any input).
candidate_issues.task_evidence: What is the minimum total cost s he has to pay on the first stage to guarantee his own win independently of the integers Vasily puts on the second stage?
